title: Observation of an emergent energy scale close to dimensional reduction in a quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet
authors: Anneke Reinold, Laur Peedu, Kirill Amelin, Urmas Nagel, Toomas Rõõm, Sven Luther, Hannes Kühne, Dirk Wulferding, Kingshuk Mukhuti, Maarten W. de Dreu, Peter C. M. Christianen, Dennis Kudlacik, Dmitri Yakovlev, Zhiying Zhao, Taro Nakajima, Yoshimitsu Kohama, Thomas Lorenz, Franco Lisandrini, Corinna Kollath, Marcin Raczkowski, Fakher F. Assaad, Zhe Wang
abstract: By appropriately perturbing a critical transverse-field Ising chain away from its critical point, the system can develop a finite correlation length with a characteristic purely massive spectrum, whose ratios and correlations are precisely described by an integrable field theory and an infinite set of integrals of motion corresponding to the $E_8$ Lie algebra. In this work, we report on experimental observation of a characteristic massive spectrum close to transverse field-induced dimensional reduction in a quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet Cu$_2$(OH)$_3$Br, providing evidence for an emergent $E_8$ symmetry and the corresponding excitations of bound states in the sublattice of its ferromagnetic chains. These results demonstrate the power of integrable field theory in describing emergent many-body quantum critical phenomena in condensed matter systems.
summary: This work reports experimental evidence from the quantum magnet $	ext{Cu}_2(	ext{OH})_3	ext{Br}$ demonstrating an emergent $E_8$ symmetry near a field-induced dimensional reduction. By measuring various spectroscopic signals (THz, NMR), the authors observed characteristic energy ratios matching predictions from integrable field theory. This links complex many-body quantum critical behavior in solids to deep mathematical symmetries.
main_problem: The study aims to observe an emergent energy scale associated with an $E_8$ symmetry near a field-induced dimensional reduction transition in a quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet.
main_result: Experimental measurements of THz absorption and spectroscopic ratios confirmed the presence of characteristic energy scales matching predictions from integrable field theory, suggesting an emergent $E_8$ symmetry.
method: The research combines experimental techniques (NMR, Raman, THz spectroscopy) with theoretical modeling based on integrable field theories to analyze quantum magnetic excitations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quasi-two-dimensional spin-$1/2$ quantum magnet $	ext{Cu}_2(	ext{OH})_3	ext{Br}$, which features coupled ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic spin chains. The theoretical framework models its behavior near a critical point perturbed by an external magnetic field.
key_observables: Spin-lattice relaxation rate ($1/T_1$), NMR line splitting, Raman scattering intensity, THz absorption coefficient ($\Delta\alpha/\omega$), and the ratio of excitation frequencies ($m_2/m_1$).
important_parameters: Applied magnetic field ($B$) along the $b$-axis, critical fields ($B_c \approx 16.3	ext{ T}$), saturation field ($B_s \approx 95	ext{ T}$), and temperatures near phase transitions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed spectral features can be accurately described by an integrable Toda field theory associated with $E_8$ symmetry, particularly in the regime approaching dimensional reduction.
figures_summary: Figures show magnetization curves defining critical fields; spectroscopic data (NMR, Raman, THz) track changes across phase transitions; Figure 4 specifically plots the ratio $m_2/m_1$ reaching the golden ratio at $9.8	ext{ T}$ and displays corresponding energy spectra.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the magnetic structure and field-induced dimensional reduction via magnetization measurements, then uses multiple spectroscopic probes (NMR, Raman, THz) to track excitations across this transition, culminating in the identification of an $E_8$-predicted signature (the golden ratio) in the low-energy spectrum.
why_interesting: The connection between a measurable condensed matter phenomenon (magnetic excitation spectra) and highly abstract mathematical structures like $E_8$ symmetry via integrable field theory is a powerful demonstration of emergent order, relevant to understanding complex many-body quantum dynamics.
